newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco de Boston won't bid on Banerj sale.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Boston won't bid on Banerj sale.

text.p: Bank of Boston Brazil unit said it will not participate in the privatization auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj and its insurer next Tuesday.

Banco de Boston, which had prequalified to bid on the Banerj sell-off, decided not to take part in the auction based on an accurate examination of the state bank's client portfolio and of the location of its 200 branches.

Banerj and its insurance company will be sold off for a minimum price of 436.693 million reais and 43.310 million reais, respectively, at a closed-envelope privatization auction on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ).
Investors will be required to buy the bank and the insurer together.
Other investors prequalified are BBA Creditanstalt, Banco CCF do Brasil, Banco Itau, Bradesco, Companhia de Investimentos Latino-Americana and U.S. General Electric Capital Corporation.

Health insurance firm Golden Cross, which prequalified only to participate in Banerj Seguros' selloff and was required to join forces with one of the other bidders to buy the company, was reported to also have given up to take part in the auction.
